q: Does the Hellmann-Feynman derivative recipe hold up when extended to the paper's second-order derivatives (Hessian and polarizability alpha_ZZ), or does the ~10^-5 Ha/A residual seen at first order compound into chemically-significant error at second order?
basis: This replication only exercised first-order derivatives (dE/dR). The paper's C5 (Newton's method) and Fig. 5 alpha_ZZ curves depend on the Hessian recipe, and the observed 10^3x accuracy penalty of HF vs FD at first order was noted but not extrapolated. Higher-order derivatives amplify state-fidelity errors quadratically.
next_steps: Extend the vqe_h2_gradients.py script with a second central-difference layer to compute d^2E/dR^2 via VQE-FD and via the paper's Hessian formula (Eq. 6-7); compare against classical FCI Hessian from PySCF. Additionally implement alpha_ZZ = d^2E/dF_Z^2 under a static electric field perturbation and compare to the paper's Fig. 5 curve at 3-5 field strengths. Free-endpoint: local classical sim only.

q: Does the paper's derivative framework work with adaptive ansatze (ADAPT-VQE, TETRIS-ADAPT) whose parameter count grows during optimization, or does parameter-shift-rule breakage when the ansatz structure changes mid-optimization invalidate the gradient recipe?
basis: The paper uses a fixed UCCSD-restricted ansatz throughout. Adaptive ansatze (Grimsley et al. 2019, Anastasiou et al. 2022) have become the practical VQE default post-2022 because they mitigate barren plateaus, but they add/remove operators during optimization, which raises well-defined derivative-continuity questions the paper does not address.
next_steps: Reimplement the H2/STO-3G experiment using PennyLane's ADAPT-VQE workflow (qml.AdaptiveOptimizer + operator pool from qml.qchem.excitations); at each ADAPT growth step compute VQE-FD, VQE-HF, and PySCF-FCI gradients and check consistency. Free-endpoint: local classical sim.

q: How does the finite-difference gradient degrade under realistic hardware shot noise, and at what shot budget does VQE-FD lose its ~10^-8 Ha/A advantage over Hellmann-Feynman?
basis: The 10^3x FD-vs-HF accuracy gap observed here is entirely a statevector-simulator artifact. Under finite-shot sampling, VQE-FD suffers from doubled sampling variance (two shifted expectations subtracted) that will dominate at moderate shot counts, potentially flipping the ordering. The paper's Section III.C discusses measurement counts but stops short of a shot-noise crossover analysis.
next_steps: Rerun the 5-point gradient scan on PennyLane's default.mixed device or via qml.sample with shot counts in {10^3, 10^4, 10^5, 10^6}, measure gradient variance for both VQE-FD and VQE-HF, and locate the crossover shot count. Optionally add a depolarizing-noise model at p in {1e-4, 1e-3}. Free-endpoint: local classical sim.

q: Can the paper's transition-state search recipe (Fig. 6b, H+H2 symmetric TS at (0.936, 0.936) A) be reproduced end-to-end using a partitioned Rational Function Optimizer (P-RFO) that requires eigenvector-following on the VQE Hessian, and does the VQE Hessian's spectral gap resolve the correct imaginary mode?
basis: Saddle-point search is the paper's most demanding claim (C7, not exercised here) because it requires (i) a reliable Hessian, (ii) discrimination between reactive and non-reactive modes via eigenvector-following, and (iii) initial-guess sensitivity that gradient-only optimization does not face. Skipping it left the verdict conditional on extra machinery.
next_steps: Extend the code to a 3-atom Hamiltonian (H3 linear, STO-3G, ~6-8 qubits) using qml.qchem.molecular_hamiltonian; write a P-RFO driver on top of the existing gradient+Hessian VQE stack; seed from the symmetric guess (0.936, 0.936) A and verify convergence to a first-order saddle with one imaginary mode aligned to the reaction coordinate. Free-endpoint: local classical sim (H3 STO-3G is still classically tractable).

q: Does the derivative recipe compose with a QM/MM or DMET embedding, i.e. do the correct effective forces on the quantum subsystem's atoms arise when the Hamiltonian includes environment-derived one- and two-electron integrals that themselves depend on the geometry?
basis: The paper treats the isolated H2 Hamiltonian and never asks whether the Hellmann-Feynman machinery survives when the embedding potential is also R-dependent (which introduces a Pulay-force-analog missing-term that classical embedding methods have to explicitly account for). This is the natural bridge from a toy H2 derivative demo to any realistic biomolecular VQE application.
next_steps: Set up a minimal H2-in-a-point-charge-field toy embedding (two static +/-0.1e point charges at fixed positions), compute d E_VQE / d R_H including the field-modified Hamiltonian, and compare against a numerical gradient of the same setup; check whether ignoring dH_environment/dR introduces a systematic shift and quantify it. Free-endpoint: local classical sim; extends existing scripts with a background-charge term in molecular_hamiltonian.
